items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: Yeah, I made a record with him. I sure did, I swear to God.

ctx.x: Did you make some records with Big Bill Bruinsy, the blues singer? Did you ever play on Big Bill? Big Bill, the blues singer.

Oh, yeah. I made a record with him by the, she's the trucking mother for you. Oh, yeah. Yeah, I made a record with him. I sure did, I swear to God. She's the trucking mother for you. Well, you couldn't forget that. No, no.
Well, so I made that in Chicago. Yeah. I thought you were on some of those. Did you make very many with him or just a couple?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: No, I just made records with him.

ctx.x: but there were two, three nightclubs in there. Oh, I see. Did you ever work any jobs with Big Bill?

No, I just made records with him. I see. When were you with Ma Rainey? Oh boy, that was when I, well I'll tell how this worked. Now Ma Rainey joined the Mac and Mac show, singing the blues, took her for the blues singer. And that's how I worked with her. When she got her own show, you know, late on I didn't work with her, I was still on the show. But I played with her with Mac and Mac.
And when you worked with Jelly Roll, would you work all year round?
